name: Database schema: `state`
desc:
The schema of the SQLite database browl calls `state`, which holds the app's own persistent state. These pages are generated from the code by [tbls](https://github.com/k1LoW/tbls) (`make schema-docs`; overview in [docs/SCHEMA.md](../../SCHEMA.md)): edit `.tbls/state.yml`, not them.

browl keeps this SQLite file, `DATA_DIR/state.sqlite3`, for the load job's state (stage, generation numbers, errors), shared by all the app's workers, the admins added in the UI, and when accounts signed out. It's authoritative and persistent, and migrates forward from its recorded version when browl starts ([DESIGN.md 2.4](../../DESIGN.md#24-load-pipeline)).

tables.name: job
tables.comment: The latest load job (browl.jobs.JobState), at most one row: each job replaces the previous one's. Times are ISO 8601 with a time zone.

columns.name: id
columns.comment: Always 1, so the table has at most one row.

columns.name: generation
columns.comment: The job's generation number, one more than the previous job's.

columns.name: stage
columns.comment: The stage the job is in, or reached (ready), or failed in (browl.jobs.Stage).

columns.name: started_at
columns.comment: When the job started.

columns.name: finished_at
columns.comment: When it reached ready or failed; NULL while it runs.

columns.name: failed_stage
columns.comment: The stage it failed in; NULL unless it failed.

columns.name: reason
columns.comment: Why it failed, cut to MAX_REASON_CHARS; NULL unless it failed.

columns.name: ready_generation
columns.comment: The generation of the latest job that reached ready, this one or an earlier one; NULL if none has.

columns.name: reasoner
columns.comment: The reasoner the admin chose (browl.jobtypes.Reasoner); 'none' skips the reasoning stage.

columns.name: upload_name
columns.comment: The uploaded file's name, as the admin's browser gave it; NULL if none.

columns.name: upload_syntax
columns.comment: The file's syntax, e.g. 'RDF/XML'.

columns.name: upload_bytes
columns.comment: The file's size; while uploading, or after a failed upload, how much arrived.

columns.name: imports
columns.comment: The ontology's imports, direct and indirect, as a JSON list of browl.jobtypes.ImportResult; '[]' until the imports stage lists them.

columns.name: triples
columns.comment: How many triples the store's default graph holds once loaded, the ontology without its imports.

columns.name: prefixes
columns.comment: The prefixes the ontology file declares, as a JSON object of name to namespace IRI, for CURIEs; '{}' until the loading stage reads them.

columns.name: stage_started_at
columns.comment: When the current stage started (P-31); NULL in a row stored before it was recorded.

columns.name: stage_seconds
columns.comment: How long each stage that ended took, in seconds, as a JSON object of stage (browl.jobs.Stage) to seconds, the stage the job failed in included; '{}' before any has ended.

columns.name: detail
columns.comment: What the running stage is doing, e.g. 'Checking for unsatisfiable classes', recorded at most every PROGRESS_S (P-31); NULL if it hasn't said, and once it ends.

columns.name: fraction
columns.comment: How far the running stage has got, from 0 to 1; NULL if it can't tell, and once it ends.

columns.name: detail_iri
columns.comment: The IRI the running stage is working on, e.g. the import being fetched (P-31), kept apart from detail because only the admin status shows it, as the "loading" page is public; NULL if none, and once the stage ends.

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE job (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (id = 1),
        generation INTEGER NOT NULL,
        stage TEXT NOT NULL,
        started_at TEXT NOT NULL,
        finished_at TEXT,
        failed_stage TEXT,
        reason TEXT,
        ready_generation INTEGER
    , reasoner TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none', upload_name TEXT, upload_syntax TEXT, upload_bytes INTEGER, imports TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', triples INTEGER, prefixes TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', stage_started_at TEXT, stage_seconds TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', detail TEXT, fraction REAL, detail_iri TEXT)

tables.name: admin
tables.comment: Admins added in the UI (DESIGN.md 2.11): a signed-in user whose verified email is here, or in SEED_ADMINS, is an admin. P-22 creates the table; P-23's admins page manages it.

columns.name: email
columns.comment: The admin's email address in its canonical form, which sign-ins are matched by (browl.admins.canonical_email): lowercased, and for Gmail without the dots in its local part.

columns.name: display_email
columns.comment: The admin's email address as it was added, lowercased, to show.

columns.name: added_at
columns.comment: When the admin was added, ISO 8601 with a time zone.

columns.name: added_by
columns.comment: The email address of the admin who added them, as they signed in; NULL if added with AUTH_DISABLED, or before P-23.

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE "admin" (
        email TEXT PRIMARY KEY CHECK (email = lower(email)),
        display_email TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (display_email = lower(display_email)),
        added_at TEXT NOT NULL,
        added_by TEXT
    )

tables.name: sign_out
tables.comment: When each account last signed out (DESIGN.md 2.11), admin or not: a session for that email that started at or before then is refused, so signing out ends the account's sessions on every device.

columns.name: email
columns.comment: The account's email address in its canonical form (browl.admins.canonical_email).

columns.name: signed_out_at
columns.comment: When it last signed out, ISO 8601 with a time zone.

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE "sign_out" (
        email TEXT PRIMARY KEY CHECK (email = lower(email)),
        signed_out_at TEXT NOT NULL
    )
